criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`. A test in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs builds fixture reading records where rule A refuses 3 first readings and 1 second reading, and rule B refuses 1 first reading. It asserts that the status output reports, per rule, the first-refusal count and the second-refusal count, over at most the last 50 readings.
criteria.evidence: I ran it with `--release`. The plain debug command failed to compile because the shared target dir held a stale `athena-data` build from Athena's revert run, which is newer than these sources. That is a problem with the environment, not the candidate; the release build compiled the candidate's athena-data. 62 tests passed, among them `each_rule_is_reported_with_its_first_and_second_refusal_counts`. Its fixture has check_governance_coverage refusing 3 first readings and 1 re-read, and check_code_survey refusing 1. It asserts the counts [(A,3,1),(B,1,0)] and that `text()` prints `check_governance_coverage: 3 first · 1 second` and `check_code_survey: 1 first · 0 second`. `athena_status_reports_the_counts_from_the_committed_invocation_records` commits these fixtures as invocation records and gets the same stats from the real `Athena::status()`. The 'fails without' run Athena recorded fails to compile with the fix reverted.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core status`. A test with fixture records of more than 50 readings asserts that only the most recent 50 are counted.
criteria.evidence: `only_the_newest_fifty_first_readings_are_counted` passed. It builds 55 first readings, where job id order runs opposite to time order. With the 5 oldest refused it gets first_readings == 50 and no rules. With 5 of the newest also refused, it counts exactly 5. `a_re_read_belongs_to_the_window_of_its_first_reading` also passed.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core hestia`. A test in crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs asserts that the sweep flags a rule refusing more than 30% of first readings. The flag names the rule and its most common refusal text. The same test asserts that a rule at or under 30% is not flagged.

findings.summary: Only the first refusing rule is recorded per reading, so later rules in the `refusing_check` order are under-counted.
findings.evidence: `refusing_check` returns at the first `step!` that fails, and `read_once` stores that one rule. The request's own example ('three corrections to satisfy two rules in turn') is a case where a second rule was hidden behind the first. The candidate documents this limit in the ReadingRuleStats docs and the CHANGELOG, so the figures are not misleading. A truer measure would record every rule that would refuse a refused first reading, by running the remaining checks for measurement only, without changing the gate.
findings.location: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs read_once (refusing_check short-circuit); crates/athena-core/src/status.rs ReadingRuleStats docs

findings.summary: `athena status` lists only rules that refused at least one reading in the window. Rules with zero refusals are not shown with 0/0.
findings.evidence: `rules` is built only from refusals seen in the window. The request asks for the counts 'per reading rule'. A reader can infer zero for an absent rule, but listing every `step!` rule with its counts would make the report complete.

summary: The change passes: all 8 acceptance criteria are met, and nothing I found is blocker or major. Nothing recorded which rule refused a reading, so the change adds an optional `reading_attempt` field to reader invocation records. It holds the attempt number (1 or 2) and, when a rule refused the reading, the rule's name and its redacted refusal text. `athena status` uses it to show, per rule, how many first readings it refused and how many second readings it still refused, over the newest 50 first readings. `athena hestia sweep` gets a `reading-rule-refusals` check. It flags a rule that refused more than 30% of first readings (`REFUSAL_FLAG_PERCENT`), naming the rule and its most common refusal text. It flags nothing, and does not report the rules as healthy, when the window holds fewer than 10 first readings (`MIN_FIRST_READINGS`). I ran the targeted tests myself: athena-core `status` (62 passed), `hestia` (77 passed) and `refused` (62 passed), and all of athena-data (192 + 3 passed). I had to add `--release` to these runs. The shared target dir held a stale athena-data build from Athena's revert run, which made the debug build fail to compile. That is a problem with the environment, not with the candidate. For fmt, clippy and the full test suite I rely on Athena's recorded CI passes. The real records have no `reading_attempt` yet, so the status section and the sweep check stay empty until new readings are recorded. Three findings, none blocking: (1, minor) only the first rule that refuses a reading is recorded, so rules later in the check order are under-counted; the docs and CHANGELOG say so. (2, minor) rules with zero refusals are not listed. (3, nit) some planned, necessary files are outside the expected-deliverables list.
